status_summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644, Public Law 119-101) became law on 2026-07-11 without the President's signature. Its text contains no provision preempting local zoning: Section 107 directs HUD to publish nonbinding zoning frameworks and bars adverse HUD action against a state or locality that declines them, Section 207 creates competitive planning and implementation grants, and Section 208 creates an Innovation Fund authorized at 200 million dollars a year for FY2027 through FY2031 that rewards housing supply growth and states that it gives HUD no power to mandate, supersede or preempt local zoning or land use policy. Per CRS, Section 213 cuts CDBG allocations by 10 percent from FY2029 for entitlement communities with below-median housing growth improvement, which adds federal fiscal pressure on local land use. Executive Order 14394 (published 2026-03-18) directed HUD to issue voluntary best practices for state and local governments, including by-right single-family development, without preempting local authority, and an undated HUD page now lists such best practices. HUD withdrew a 2016 joint statement on land use law and the Fair Housing Act in a notice published 2026-07-17.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14394 was published, directing HUD to issue voluntary state and local best practices on housing regulation, including by-right single-family development.

uncertainties: The enrolled text of Public Law 119-101 was read in review on govinfo.gov through Section 212 (Sections 107, 207 and 208 confirmed); the HTML, PDF and USLM copies all cut off before Section 213 in the fetch tool, so Section 213 rests on CRS R49354, which was read in its first 100,000 characters in review. Provisions such as Sections 103 and 206 were not examined for zoning effects beyond their headings. The HUD page titled State and Local Best Practices for Home Construction cites Executive Order 14394 and recommends by-right single-family development, but it carries no date, so it is not a dated timeline event; the order set a 60-day deadline of about 2026-05-12. The HUD withdrawal notice states an effective date of 2025-09-25, earlier than its publication. The classification is partial because the law avoids preemption but adds incentives and a CDBG adjustment that push toward zoning change.
